sub_senses.meaning: to leave unconsumed, un-done, to spare

quotations.old_english: Hé ne belǽfde náne láte cuce
Nán hǽðengyld se hagol ne belǽfde
Þone sǽdere hé belǽfde ús tó sécenne
Næs nán ele belǽfed tó his gebróðra bricum
Án of him ne beláf (-lǽfde, MS. C)
Hé hét ácwellan þá crístenan, wolde þ-bar; nán man ne belǽfde crísten

source_text: be-lǽfan. Substitute: I. trans, (I) to leave, be survived by:--Hé bearn ne belǽfð, Hml. Th. ii. 146, 20. (2) to leave unconsumed, un-done, to spare:--Hé ne belǽfde náne láte cuce non dimiserunt ullas reliquias, Jos. 10, 28. Nán hǽðengyld se hagol ne belǽfde, Hml. S. 4, 427: Hml. Th. ii. 194, 2. Þone sǽdere hé belǽfde ús tó sécenne, 90, 8. Næs nán ele belǽfed tó his gebróðra bricum, 178, 20. II. intrans. To remain [for intrans. use in later English v. N. E. D. s. v. bielieve]:-- Án of him ne beláf (-lǽfde, MS. C), Ps. Spl. 105, II. Hé hét ácwellan þá crístenan, wolde þ-bar; nán man ne belǽfde crísten, Hml. S. 29, 202. [Goth. bi-laibjan to leave.]
